title: Globe-CraterSAM: a training-free generalizable framework for mapping sub-kilometer martian craters
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Robust reinforcement learning multi-baseline phase unwrapping algorithm with JPEG-LS
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Multi-baseline (MB) phase unwrapping (PU) breaks through the limitations of the phase continuity assumption, but existing MBPU algorithms cannot adapt well to noisy environments. A robust reinforcement learning integer programming multi-baseline PU algorithm with JPEG-LS (RL-MBPU) is proposed. First, the cutting plane–pure integer programming cut-selection process is formulated as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem. An efficacy-guided imitation strategy is used to initialize an MBPU-structure-aware single-cut policy, which is further optimized by an actor–critic method using Cut-PAR2-based trajectory returns to reduce the root-node proof cost. Finally, the initial ambiguity number solution is corrected using dynamic median edge detector based on JPEG-LS, and the PU is completed by using the prediction of the left, top, and top-left neighbors of the current pixel and combining it with the local gradient threshold determination. In both simulation and real data experiments, the RL-MBPU algorithm demonstrated stable PU performance, including computational efficiency and noise robustness for interferograms of different sizes. Compared with the minimum-cost flow and cutting plane–pure integer programming algorithms, the RL-MBPU algorithm reduces the root mean square error by approximately 61.2% and 14.5%, respectively, while improving efficiency by approximately 54.1% and 42.4%, respectively. This can further support high-precision interferometric synthetic aperture radar applications.

title: Airborne observatory for high-resolution land surface temperature and spectral emissivity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: LexSign: Learning Sign Language from Lexical Descriptions
30-meter land surface temperature from Landsat via progressive self-training downscaling
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) is a critical parameter for characterizing surface energy balance and hydrothermal processes. While Landsat has provided invaluable LST observations at medium spatial resolution for over 40 years, its native spatial resolution of thermal bands (e.g., 100 m) remains insufficient compared to its 30 m optical bands, failing to meet the demands of fine-scale studies. To address this issue, this study proposes a progressive self-training framework for downscaling Landsat LST to 30 m without relying on fine-scale ground truth, while requiring minimal external data dependence. The framework progressively optimizes a cross-modal fusion network to refine thermal details in a coarse-to-fine manner, characterized by one pre-training stage and two fine-tuning stages. This network leverages a cross-modal dictionary attention mechanism combined with a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture to effectively extract complementary information between LST and auxiliary variables across multiple spatial resolutions. Quantitative ablation analyses demonstrate that the fusion design and auxiliary variable combination effectively reduce downscaling errors. In parallel, a frequency-domain guidance strategy, implemented at both the network structure and loss-function levels, is introduced to enhance structural fidelity and suppress artifact accumulation during progressive refinement. Ablation of the high-frequency structural loss further demonstrates its effectiveness in reconstructing crisp fine-scale thermal textures. Spatial validation against SDGSAT-1 30 m LST and temporal validation using in situ measurements confirm its reliability and accuracy, yielding a station-averaged RMSE of 3.465 K and an R 2 of 0.909, compared with 4.195 K and 0.861 for the official cubic interpolation product. Comparisons with existing methods further demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively reconstructs fine-scale thermal patterns while preserving spatial heterogeneity. Overall, the framework provides a stable pathway for enhancing the spatial resolution of Landsat LST, offering fine-resolution data support for fine-scale surface process studies and localized environmental monitoring.

title: AeroReformer2: Spoken-query referring segmentation for aerial images
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Spoken queries provide a natural, hands-free way to identify targets in dense remote-sensing imagery. Existing referring segmentation benchmarks in this domain accept only written expressions. We introduce VoiceAeroRef, a spoken-query benchmark derived from RISBench. It adds synthetic speech with diverse accents and voices while preserving the source images, masks, and data splits. A hard test set combines rotor, wind, and mixed interference with three signal-to-noise levels. We also propose AeroReformer2, a bilateral network for efficient speech-conditioned segmentation. The network retains speech tokens and conditions visual features at two scales through kernel linear attention. This avoids constructing a dense speech–visual affinity matrix. A detail path and a high-resolution refinement head preserve object boundaries. On the clean test split, the Swin-Base version achieves a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 62.09% and an overall intersection over union (oIoU) of 68.22%. These scores exceed those of the strongest audio-adapted remote-sensing baseline by 5.38 and 2.08 percentage points, respectively. The model also achieves the highest mIoU on the hard test set, at 54.09%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to introduce a benchmark and model for full-sentence spoken-query referring segmentation in remote-sensing imagery. The project, along with code and dataset, is available at https://lironui.github.io/AeroReformer2/ .

title: Quantifying anisotropic impacts of LCZ landscape patterns on NO2 variabilities in the Yangtze River Delta, China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Urban landscape patterns strongly affect air quality, yet existing studies often neglect anisotropic processes, rely on arbitrary fixed-radius buffers, and lack standardized classification frameworks. To overcome these limitations, we developed a novel analytical framework that integrates high-accuracy Local Climate Zone (LCZ) classification, multi-scale spatial modeling, and a shape-adaptive influence zone. Central to this framework is the Adaptive Directionally Weighted Sector Influence Zone (ADWSIZ), a new method that explicitly captures the directional heterogeneity of landscape effects on pollutants. Applied to station-based NO 2 measurements in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) urban agglomeration, we used multi-scale Geographically Weighted Ridge Regression (GWRR) to identify a 4000 m circular buffer as the optimal modeling scale, revealing a clear decoupling from the intrinsic static LCZ pattern scale (approximately 1000 m). Building upon this optimal distance, the ADWSIZ model was developed to refine the influence zone’s shape. The application of ADWSIZ improved model performance (Adjusted R 2 : 0.464 → 0.506 ; RMSE: 2.950 → 2.834 µg/m 3 ) and reduced residual spatial autocorrelation. Our findings highlight that the anisotropic influence of features like industrial land and compact high-rise fabrics is a critical, previously underexplored factor in explaining NO 2 variation. This study establishes a replicable and transferable methodology that advances the conceptualization of influence zones from simple distance-based buffers to scale- and shape-adaptive forms, offering a robust tool for refining spatial coupling analyses between urban morphology and air pollutants.
